sections.profile_subtitle: From systems & networks to Salesforce development
sections.bridge_body: On the Légarant-AXG deployment — my RNCP Level 6 capstone project — I didn't just write the Apex REST endpoints on the Salesforce side — I also built and deployed the Heroku application that consumes them: a Node.js/PostgreSQL API, two isolated environments connected by a Heroku pipeline, Heroku Connect configured object by object, down to the deployment runbook. A Salesforce-only profile would have stopped at the Apex layer and handed the infrastructure piece to someone else, with the usual risk of decisions made without knowing the constraints on the other side. An infra-only profile could have deployed the Heroku app, but not designed the Apex External ID trigger or the Matching Rule that stops duplicates at the source. Delivering both together removed the usual back-and-forth between Salesforce and DevOps teams — the staging environment existed before the first line of Apex was written, not after. This project, not a badge, is the proof that Salesforce, infrastructure, and security aren't two overlapping résumés — they're one person making both decisions at once. The same reflex shows up, in a form you can verify, in the MediCare Solutions validation pipeline (work in progress): every Pull Request is validated against the Salesforce org by GitHub Actions, with server-to-server JWT Bearer authentication and a private key wiped from the runner after every run — DevOps discipline applied to how Salesforce releases ship, not just how they're built.

sections.security_body: STRIDE threat modeling, CVSS scoring, a state machine with per-severity SLAs, triage synced in real time with the public NVD API — not one more line on a skills list, this is the densest sub-cluster on the portfolio: {count} projects out of {total}, spanning both tracks.

profile.title: From systems & networks to Salesforce development
profile.p1: Salesforce developer with 3 years of professional experience and a strong IT infrastructure background — foundations that make a real difference on complex projects.
profile.p2: I started my career on the infrastructure side — internship at MIDRANGE GROUP (Feb – May 2023) as a junior systems & network administrator: support for 50+ workstations, deployment of 264 Dell machines (200 of them via Windows Autopilot), Windows Server 2022 administration (AD DS, DNS, DHCP, GPO), PfSense/Squid, Acronis, Datto RMM. This hands-on experience taught me how systems behave in real life and why solid foundations matter.
profile.p3: From Oct. 2023 to Oct. 2025, I worked as a Salesforce Developer at LD Digitales (remote) while earning the Développeur Concepteur Logiciel title (RNCP Level 6) from OpenClassrooms. I built and maintained 10+ Apex classes, created 20+ automation Flows (reducing manual workload by ~30%), designed reusable LWC components, and implemented CI/CD pipelines with Salesforce CLI.
profile.p4: I do my best work in environments that value autonomy, transparency, and continuous learning. My goal is to contribute to ambitious Salesforce and IT Ops projects — in France or internationally, within distributed teams.
profile.p1_salesforce: Salesforce developer & consultant: I design reliable, secure, maintainable solutions with a strong focus on user experience and delivery quality.
profile.p2_salesforce: I work with Apex, Flows, data models, security (permission sets, sharing), and CI/CD pipelines (Salesforce CLI, GitHub Actions) to ship cleanly to production.
profile.p3_salesforce: My systems & DevOps background helps me approach Salesforce with an operations mindset: observability, risk management, documentation, and automation—so solutions stay robust over time.
profile.p4_salesforce: Full-time Salesforce Developer at LD Digitales since October 2025, after two years as a work-study developer at the same company: 3 years of production Salesforce experience. The Legarant-AXG project (Heroku Connect, environment management, traceable production releases) remains the clearest proof of that Salesforce/infra crossover: not an application layer sitting on infrastructure someone else manages, but the same person on both sides. On the academic side, I hold the RNCP Level 6 (Bac+3/4 equivalent) 'Développeur Concepteur Logiciel' title, Salesforce specialization (OpenClassrooms, 2025), and an active Trailhead profile (Expeditioner rank, 94 badges) — the Salesforce certifications (Platform Foundations, Administrator, App Builder, Platform Developer I) are scheduled for November 2026.
profile.p1_itops: IT Ops & DevOps: during my two one-month internships at MIDRANGE GROUP (Feb–May 2023), I remotely monitored 550+ devices through Datto RMM, handled 316 support tickets and deployed 264 Dell workstations (Windows Autopilot, Sysprep image, NIST 800-88 certified wipe).
profile.p2_itops: During my TAI and TSSR training (Greta du Val-d'Oise), I installed and administered Windows Server environments — AD DS, DNS, DHCP, GPO, pfSense/Squid filtering, virtualization — documenting every procedure as a runbook.
profile.p3_itops: I pay close attention to security and continuity: 85 Acronis backup alerts triaged during the internship, and personal labs (honeypot, traffic analysis, vulnerability management) to keep those reflexes sharp outside of work.
profile.p4_itops: Full-time Salesforce Developer at LD Digitales — my IT Ops & DevOps skills, built during my internship at MIDRANGE GROUP and in training, remain fully available in a hybrid role. The Legarant-AXG project (the Apex REST layer AND its companion Heroku app, deployment runbook included) shows this crossover isn't just a resume line: the same person designs the Salesforce integration and runs the infrastructure it depends on. On the academic side, I hold the RNCP Level 6 (Bac+3/4 equivalent) 'Développeur Concepteur Logiciel' title (OpenClassrooms, 2025).

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.analyticsBody: This site uses Umami Cloud in production to measure audience (page views, CV downloads, contact clicks) and Core Web Vitals, i.e. the performance real visitors actually experience. Umami sets no cookies; statistics are aggregated and anonymous, and data is hosted in the European Union (Frankfurt). This service is disabled in development.
privacy.cookiesBody: No marketing or tracking cookies are set. The language preference is stored in the URL (e.g. /en/, /fr/) and not in a cookie. A functional 'track' cookie (1-year lifetime) and a matching browser local-storage entry only remember which profile is displayed (Salesforce or IT Ops); they contain no personal data. Vercel may set technical cookies for infrastructure purposes (CDN, DDoS protection). The Calendly booking widget is only loaded if you open it; Calendly's own cookie policy then applies.
privacy.formBody: When you submit the contact form, the data you enter — name, email, topic, message — is forwarded by email via Formhook (an EU-hosted email delivery service) to handle your request. The site keeps no copy of this data on its servers. Your IP address is used only transiently to rate-limit abusive submissions (anti-spam) and is not stored with your message.
privacy.retention: Retention: the site does not store contact messages. Once forwarded by email, your message is retained in the mailbox under normal email practice; you may request its deletion at any time by contacting me.
privacy.rightsBody: In accordance with applicable data protection regulations (GDPR), you have the right to access, rectify, request deletion of, and obtain portability of your personal data.
privacy.processorsBody: Data collected through this website is processed by the following sub-processors: Formhook (contact-form email delivery — EU-hosted), Vercel (hosting and CDN — United States), Supabase (testimonials submitted via the dedicated form, and service-status / incident history — United States, GDPR compliance via Standard Contractual Clauses), Upstash (anti-spam rate limiting, per-IP counter — ephemeral data). hybrid.metaTitle: Hybrid Salesforce + Infrastructure profile — Aïcha Imène DAHOUMANE
hybrid.metaDescription: Three concrete cases where solving the problem requires the combination of Salesforce + infrastructure + security — not their juxtaposition. Heroku↔Salesforce data migration, DevOps discipline applied to Apex releases, integration attack surface modelled with STRIDE.
hybrid.h1: Where Salesforce, infrastructure and security are one head, not two
hybrid.lead: I'm not a Salesforce developer who knows servers, nor a sysadmin who knows Salesforce. I solve cross-cutting problems that a single specialist — on either side — would handle more slowly, less well, or not at all: both layers' decisions are made at the same time, by the same person, before the usual back-and-forth between teams even starts. The evidence cited below comes from training and personal projects; each page states its type and period.
hybrid.scenariosTitle: Three cases where the combination changes the outcome

scenarios.title: Heroku ↔ Salesforce data migration, with a field mobile app
scenarios.problem: An insurer acquires a competitor: the acquired CRM's data has to flow into Salesforce (one-way), and field agents need a mobile app that reads and writes against the same org.
scenarios.solo: A Salesforce profile stops at the Apex REST layer and hands off the Heroku infrastructure — integration decisions are made without knowing the constraints on the other side. An infrastructure profile deploys the Heroku app, but designs neither the External ID Apex trigger nor the Matching Rule that stop duplicates at the source.
scenarios.mine: Both: the Apex REST endpoints, the Node.js/PostgreSQL app that consumes them, Heroku Connect configured object by object, two isolated environments linked by a pipeline, right down to the deployment runbook. The staging environment existed before the first line of Apex was written — not after.
scenarios.sector: Insurance and finance: reconciling two customer books where a duplicate isn't an inconvenience but an orphan file and a compliance risk.

scenarios.title: DevOps discipline applied to Salesforce releases
scenarios.problem: Shipping Salesforce changes repeatedly without breaking production, with auditable traceability on every go-live.
scenarios.solo: A Salesforce profile can code the feature, but deploys via manual Change Set, with no documented rollback procedure. A DevOps profile can build a pipeline, but doesn't know the pitfalls of deploying Salesforce metadata — no native undo, dependency order between components.
scenarios.mine: Real DevOps discipline — automated validation of every Pull Request against the org, server-to-server JWT Bearer authentication, a private key wiped from the runner after every run, a documented SFDX rollback procedure — applied to how Salesforce releases are delivered, not just how they're coded.

proofs.label: MediCare Solutions — validation workflow (work in progress)

scenarios.sector: Any regulated sector — healthcare, energy, finance: every production change must be traceable and reversible, not just functional.

scenarios.title: An integration's attack surface, modelled with STRIDE
scenarios.problem: A Salesforce integration exposes REST endpoints: who calls them, with which token, what happens if the flow is replayed or hijacked?
scenarios.solo: A Salesforce developer documents the endpoint and the Permission Sets. A pentester audits the API — but doesn't know which Permission Set, which CRUD/FLS check or which Sharing Rule actually closes the gap on the Salesforce side.
scenarios.mine: I model the attack surface with STRIDE and design the control on the Salesforce side — a dedicated integration user, an explicit Permission Set, CRUD/FLS checks, WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED — in the same sprint. The loop is closed before go-live, not three tickets later.

proofs.label: RNCP 6 training project — iDEM Connect Apex backend

scenarios.sector: Healthcare and luxury: integrations that move patient data or product provenance — where a flaw isn't a technical incident but a breach of trust.

eliminates: The back-and-forth between the Salesforce team and the infra/DevOps team on every integration decision.

Decisions made on one side without knowing the constraints of the other — a trigger designed without knowing how the infra calls it, a pipeline designed without knowing Salesforce's deployment limits.
The gap between "the API is audited" and "the control is in place": both happen in the same sprint.
hybrid.ctaText: If the role touches both Salesforce and infrastructure — integration, migration, traceable go-live, API security — that's exactly where this profile saves a team time.
